key_insight: RareDx improves rare-disease ranking by combining controlled evidence use with knowledge-graph-grounded policy optimization, helping a smaller model avoid plausible but invalid diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support diagnostic decision-making in long-tail rare cases by surfacing more accurate ranked differentials from heterogeneous medical knowledge sources.
method: RareDx-Harness standardizes diverse rare-disease cases into a shared ranked-diagnosis task.
The system compares direct inference, retrieval, adaptive tools, and structured phenotype-gene-disease reasoning over a common knowledge layer.
RareDx-KGPO trains with rewards that project predictions into a canonical disease graph and score relevance, ontology proximity, biomedical similarity, and phenotype consistency.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmarks, the Qwen3.5-9B-based system achieved 38.34 macro Hit@10 and beat GPT-5.5 by 1.60 points under the archived protocol, with a held-out routing audit showing a 6.80-point gain over Direct.
watch_item: Performance depends on controlled routing and graph-based scoring, so results may not transfer well if the knowledge base is incomplete, mismatched, or poorly maintained.
paper_title: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
